description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Representative Madeleine Dean (D-PA) criticizes the Trump Administration’s stability following the announcement that Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer will be leaving. Jane Harman, former Democratic congresswoman from California who served as Ranking Member of the House Intelligence Committee, says the US is sending “mixed messages” ahead of Iran talks by sending Vice President JD Vance to negotiate again.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer to Leave | Balance of Power: Late Edition 04/20/2026

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Air Force on Monday canceled RTX Corp.’s ground-control network for the US’s next generation of GPS satellites after years of delays and cost overruns.
title: Air Force Scraps RTX GPS Satellite Ground Control Program

description: Jane Harman, former Democratic congresswoman from California who served as Ranking Member of the House Intelligence Committee, says the US is sending “mixed messages” ahead of Iran talks by sending Vice President JD Vance to negotiate again. She also warns failure to renew FISA surveillance authorities would be “catastrophic,” and calls allegations against FBI Director Kash Patel “very alarming.” She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Harman on Iran Talks, FISA Risks

author: Ari Natter
description: US Interior Security Doug Burgum said China’s key role in supplying US solar developments necessitates a more rigorous review process to ferret out any potential threats to national security.
title: Burgum Cites China Link in Tougher US Reviews for Solar Projects

author: Josh Sisco, Leah Nylen
description: Rapid changes in media fueled by increased use of artificial intelligence and streaming services require a “cautious humility” from antitrust enforcers as they assess whether mergers in the industry are threatening competition and consumers, a senior US Justice Department official said.
title: DOJ Signals Antitrust Shift on Media Deals as AI Alters Industry

description: Representative Madeleine Dean (D-PA) criticizes the Trump Administration’s stability following the announcement that Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer will be leaving. She goes on to state that Pete Hegseth and Kash Patel “should be very worried,” talks about how the Labor Secretary leaving impacts the budget process, and what to expect after the ceasefire ends later this week. Representative Dean speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s “Balance of Power.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Administration Not Stable: Rep. Dean on Chavez-DeRemer Leaving

author: Tyler Kendall, Catherine Lucey
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer met with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on Monday as the two countries prepare for a review of the North American trade pact, according to a readout of their meeting.
title: Greer Meets Mexico’s Sheinbaum as Teams Prepare for USMCA Review

description: On today’s Big Take podcast, Bloomberg’s Stacey Vanek Smith and Kate Sullivan break down rising US-Iran tensions, why nuclear talks and the Strait of Hormuz remain deadlocked and what it all means for potential negotiations in Islamabad. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Mixed Messaging Clouds Potential New US-Iran Talks

author: Stacey Vanek Smith, Rachael Lewis-Krisky, David Fox
description: The US and Iran are still at odds over the future of Tehran’s nuclear program and control of the Strait of Hormuz. What that friction could mean for peace talks and a looming ceasefire deadline.
title: Iran Tensions Flare Again: What’s Next for Negotiations?

author: Josh Wingrove, Laura Davison
description: Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer is departing her post, becoming the latest member of President Donald Trump’s cabinet to exit as he reshapes his team ahead of midterm elections.
title: Labor Chief Chavez-DeRemer Leaving Cabinet Amid Investigation

author: Alan Crawford, Heidi Taksdal Skjeseth
description: NATO is fighting back against Russia's submarine threat in cat-and-mouse games reminiscent of the Cold War
title: Putin’s High-Tech Russian Submarines Goad NATO Deep Below the Atlantic

author: Emily Birnbaum, Lydia Beyoud
description: Prediction markets are pouring money into Washington to defend against escalating criticism that their fast-growing platforms are contributing to a gambling explosion and enabling insider trading.
title: Prediction Markets Ramp Up Washington Lobbying to Stop US Rules

author: Nancy Cook
description: The Fed chair nominee appears in front of the Senate Banking Committee.
title: Prepping for Warsh’s High-Stakes Fed Confirmation Hearing

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss the latest developments out of Iran as President Trump says he's not likely to extend a two-week ceasfire. The S&P 500 snapped a five-day winning streak and oil moved higher as turbulence out of the region continued weighing on investors. Bloomberg News Washington and White Correspondent Jeff Mason joins to discuss President Trump's phone interview this morning. Then, Bloomberg Economics US and Canada Economist Stuart Paul previews tomorrow's Senate testimony from Federal Reserve chairman nominee Kevin Warsh. Plus, Rich Weiss of American Century Investments weighs in on his call that yield curve control is a possibility under a Warsh Fed. Finally, Bloomberg News AI Infrastructure Reporter Dina Bass on her reporting that Google is betting on new chips to boost its AI results and challenge Nvidia. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Fall, Oil Jumps on Iran Peace Deal Doubts | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 4/20/2026

author: Jim Wyss, Eric Martin
description: Cuba said it held meetings with US officials on the island in recent days as Washington pushes Havana to open up the state-controlled economy.
title: Cuba Confirms US Visit as Trump Tries to Force Change on Island

author: Josh Wingrove, Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump invoked the Defense Production Act to provide federal funds for a wide range of energy projects, as his administration faces pressure to help curb rising oil and gas costs.
title: Trump Invokes Wartime Powers to Fund New Energy Projects

author: Rachel Schilke, Maeve Sheehey
description: The House Ethics Committee gave unusual insight into its sexual misconduct investigations Monday, saying it has initiated 20 probes since 2017 while also encouraging those with knowledge of wrongdoing to come forward.
title: House Ethics Launched 20 Sexual Misconduct Probes Since 2017

author: Andra Timu, Irina Vilcu
description: Romania’s government has been thrown into turmoil after the top ruling party withdrew its support for Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, whose own bloc is now rallying to salvage his control of the four-way coalition.
title: Romania Coalition Nears Collapse as Top Party Spurns Premier

author: Carla Samon Ros
description: Final results of Peru’s presidential election are set to be pushed back by weeks as electoral authorities settle as many as a million challenged ballots, leaving the Andean country on edge over which candidate will face conservative Keiko Fujimori in a June runoff.
title: Peru’s Presidential Vote Count to Drag On Through Mid-May

author: Francesca Maglione
description: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass proposed a $14.9 billion budget on Monday, saying higher revenue collections helped ease the city’s financial strain after a roughly $1 billion deficit in the current fiscal year.
title: LA Mayor Proposes $14.9 Billion Budget as Revenue Improves

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Republican Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis of New York. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Aims to Seal Iran Deal | Balance of Power: Early Edition 4/20/2026

author: Alex Wickham, Lucy White, Joe Mayes
description: Keir Starmer did what he could on Monday to weather a parliamentary showdown on his handling of the Peter Mandelson scandal. On Tuesday, it may rest with a bureaucrat little known outside Westminster to decide his fate.
title: Starmer’s Political Fate Rests With Top UK Bureaucrat He Fired

description: Bloomberg's Jeff Mason said that the president told him that the temporary ceasefire between the US and Iran will now end Wednesday evening, but that it is unlikely to extend beyond that.  Mason said that his phone call from the President contained mixed messages, Trump's choice to add another day to the truce at odds with his stance that he will not extend it further if a deal is not reached by negotiators in Islamabad.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Ceasefire Done Weds Evening, Unlikely to Extend Further

description: Republican Representative Nicole Malliotakis said that while the US has the upper hand in negotiations with Iran, lawmakers need to be realistic about the impact constituents are feeling at home and the resulting political pressure on the Republican party.  The New York Congresswoman also said that Congress must extend the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act Section 702 because it's critically important to confronting the threat of terrorism. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He's Under 'No Pressure' to Make Quick Iran Deal

description: Wells Fargo & Co. Chief Executive Officer Charlie Scharf says Federal Reserve independence is "critically important," but he says President Donald Trump is allowed to have his own point of view. Scharf spoke Monday during an interview with David Rubenstein at the Economic Club of Washington DC. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Independence Is Critically Important, Says Wells Fargo CEO Scharf

author: Aaron Eglitis, Ott Tammik
description: Estonia’s government criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy’s warning that Russia could be preparing to attack the Baltic states, in a rare rebuke from one of Kyiv’s staunchest allies.
title: Estonia Rebuffs Ukraine’s Warnings of Russian Invasion

author: Ewa Krukowska, Andrea Palasciano, Volodymyr Verbianyi
description: Ukraine expects oil to resume flowing through the Druzhba pipeline as soon as Tuesday, clearing the way for the European Union to unblock a much-needed €90 billion ($106 billion) loan for Kyiv.
title: Ukraine Sees Druzhba Oil Return Tuesday, Paving Way for Loan

author: Greg Stohr
description: The US Supreme Court expressed little enthusiasm for curbing one of the Securities and Exchange Commission’s most important enforcement tools, as the justices weighed restricting the financial watchdog for the fourth time in a decade.
title: Supreme Court Voices Little Interest in New Curbs on SEC’s Power

description: President Donald Trump said it’s “highly unlikely” he would extend the two-week ceasefire with Iran if a deal is not reached before it ends, and said the Strait of Hormuz would remain blocked until an agreement is finalized. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran Truce Extension Unlikely, Hormuz Stays Shut

description: President Donald Trump said it’s “highly unlikely" he would extend the two-week ceasefire with Iran if no agreement is reached in time. Trump said he won't be rushed "into making a bad deal." Bloomberg's Jeff Mason spoke exclusively to President Trump on the phone Monday morning and has much more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says 'Highly Unlikely' He Extends Iran Ceasefire

author: Fadwa Hodali
description: Gaza needs an estimated $71.4 billion over the next decade to recover from two years of war that devastated most of the Palestinian territory, a new study by the European Union, United Nations and World Bank shows.
title: Gaza Needs $71 Billion Over Next Decade to Rebuild, Study Shows

description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer criticized civil servants for failing to inform him that Peter Mandelson had failed security vetting.  "I simply do not accept that Foreign Office officials could not have informed me of UKSV's recommendations whilst also maintaining the necessary confidentiality vetting requirements," Starmer told the House of Commons on Monday. "If I had known before he took up his post that UKSV recommendation was that developed vetting clearance should be denied, I would not have gone ahead with the appointment," he added. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Starmer Says Not Informed on Mandelson Failing Security Vetting

author: Myles Miller
description: FBI Director Kash Patel filed a $250 million defamation lawsuit against The Atlantic and staff writer Sarah Fitzpatrick over a story alleging excessive drinking and unexplained absences, calling the reporting “malicious lies” built on anonymous sources with partisan motives.
title: FBI Director Patel Sues Atlantic in $250 Million Defamation Case

description: Ian Bremmer, Eurasia Group president and founder, discusses the recent US military blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, where 27 vessels have been directed to turn back. This move aims to increase economic pressure on Iran, although Bremmer notes that Iran currently benefits from higher oil prices and had previously seen a suspension of US oil sanctions. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Has Already 'Blown Up' Iran Talks, Ian Bremmer Says

description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said on Monday that the recommendation from UK Security Vetting that Peter Mandelson should be denied developed vetting clearance "was information that could and should have been shared" with him "on repeated occasions." Starmer was speaking in the the House of Commons.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UK PM: Should Have Been Told About UKSV Recommendation on Mandelson
Starmer Apologizes for Appointing Mandelson (Video)

author: Andreina Itriago, Fabiola Zerpa
description: María Corina Machado said she will return to Venezuela this year, a move that will test acting President Delcy Rodríguez’s tolerance for dissent and the US commitment to back the opposition leader it once pledged to protect.
title: Machado Says She’ll Return This Year, Testing Venezuela’s Leader

author: Jeff Mason
description: President Donald Trump said it’s “highly unlikely” he would extend the two-week ceasefire with Iran if a deal is not reached before it ends, and said the Strait of Hormuz would remain blocked until an agreement is finalized.
title: Trump Says Iran Truce Extension Unlikely, Hormuz to Stay Blocked

author: Joe Mayes
description: Embattled UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer apologized for his appointment of Peter Mandelson as the UK’s ambassador to Washington, as he criticized civil servants for failing to inform him that the Labour grandee had failed security vetting.
title: Starmer Apologizes for Mandelson Appointment Amid Vetting Fury

author: S'thembile Cele
description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa urged the United Nations to reassert itself in global affairs to safeguard democracy that’s under threat from resurgent nationalism, conflict and widening inequality.
title: South Africa Slams Powerless UN as Democracy Faces Global Strain

author: Thomas Escritt
description: Hungary’s incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar said he would halt the departure from the International Criminal Court that his predecessor Viktor Orban initiated, affirming that Hungary would respect its obligation to detain leaders on its territory sought by the Hague-based tribunal.
title: Hungary Must Arrest Visiting Leaders Sought by ICC, Magyar Says

author: Tom Rees
description: The UK government will ask departments to go even further on finding savings and get a “big win” from automating swathes of the public sector, according to Treasury minister James Murray.
title: UK to Ask Departments for More Savings, Touts ‘Big Win’ From AI

description: The US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is still in place as Iran says it has no plans to send diplomats to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks. Tyler Kendall has the latest from Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Seizes Iranian Ship as Ceasefire Is Set to Expire

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: The US is willing to assist the United Arab Emirates in case the war in Iran worsens its economic outlook, though a currency-swap line most likely won’t be necessary, President Donald Trump’s top economic adviser said.
title: US Would Likely Help UAE Financially If Needed, Hassett Says

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump said a US delegation including Vice President JD Vance is en route to Pakistan for talks with Iran and is expected to land in the next few hours, after fresh tensions in the war raised doubts about further negotiations.
title: Vance on Way to Pakistan for Iran Talks, Trump Tells NY Post

author: Thomas Escritt, Andras Gergely
description: Hungary’s incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar named the key ministers for his new government who will help shoulder the task of repairing frayed European ties and relaunching a stagnant economy.
title: Magyar Unveils Cabinet Team to Lead Hungary’s Economic Reset

author: Patrick Gillespie, Michael O'Boyle
description: President Javier Milei is seeking billions in private capital to turn Argentina’s decaying freight railways into a key route for hauling grain and minerals to export ports.
title: Milei’s Auction of Argentine Railroads Risks Sidelining US-Backed Bidder

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Ilya Remeslo, a pro-Kremlin activist who said he spent time in a psychiatric hospital after lashing out at President Vladimir Putin in a series of posts on Telegram last month, has reappeared with more critical messages aimed at the Kremlin.
title: Kremlin Loyalist Who Turned on Putin Returns With More Criticism

author: Slav Okov
description: Former President Rumen Radev’s Progressive Bulgaria won 45% of the votes in Sunday’s general election, the country’s election administration said on Monday.
title: Bulgaria’s Radev Wins 45%, Gerb Has 13% With All Votes Counted

author: Jorge Valero, Misha Savic
description: The European Union is warning six candidate countries in the western Balkans that they risk losing out of €700 million ($823 million) in funding from the bloc unless they carry out required reforms by the end of June, according to a person familiar with the matter.
title: EU Warns Balkan Hopefuls That Reforms Are Needed to Access Funds

author: Patrick Van Oosterom, Charlotte Hughes-Morgan
description: The Netherlands has allocated more than €950 million ($1.1 billion) to blunt the Iran war’s economic effects on Dutch households and businesses, as it prepares for possible fuel shortages.
title: Netherlands Earmarks €1 Billion to Mitigate Iran Price Shocks

author: Foster Wong
description: China President Xi Jinping called for an immediate ceasefire and the restoration of normal transit through the Strait of Hormuz, following a turbulent weekend in the Middle East that has clouded prospects for peace talks.
title: China’s Xi Urges Ceasefire, Full Hormuz Transit in Saudi Call

description: The US navy seized an Iranian-flagged ship for the first time in its naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, dimming hopes of a breakthrough in peace talks. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Ship Seizure Dims Hopes of Iran Breakthrough

author: Lucy White
description: Nigel Farage’s anti-immigration Reform UK Party said it would review all asylum claims going back five years if it wins power at the next general election, deporting those deemed to have entered the country “illegally” or overstayed visas.
title: Farage’s Reform Proposes ICE-Style Deportation Policy for UK

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: How Tehran is sustaining a war against two stronger foes
title: Why Trump Hasn’t Been Able to Break Iran’s Regime Yet

author: Rajesh Roy
description: India Prime Minister Narendra Modi isn’t letting his failed bid to overhaul the parliament go to waste.
title: Modi Turns Women’s Bill Loss Into Campaign Weapon in West Bengal

author: Greg Ryan, Katherine Doherty
description: The Boston Marathon on Monday marks the starting gun for a pivotal tourism season in a city grappling with slowdowns in key business sectors and international travelers’ diminished appetite for visiting the US.
title: Boston Marathon Kicks Off in Key Tourism Test for World Cup Host

author: Enda Curran, Amara Omeokwe
description: Kevin Warsh has for years accused the Federal Reserve of losing its way and said it’s in desperate need of “regime change.”
title: Fed Pick Warsh to Face Senate Grilling With Confirmation in Limbo

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: The European Union’s antitrust chief has rebuffed calls for watered-down merger rules to help the bloc create its own business giants to rival US and Chinese behemoths.
title: EU Antitrust Chief Attacks Push to Loosen Merger Rules

author: Anuchit Nguyen
description: Thailand will press ahead with a long-standing plan to link the Indian and Pacific oceans, bypassing the Malacca Strait, after tensions over the Strait of Hormuz highlighted the strategic value of key shipping routes, a senior minister said.
title: Hormuz Crisis Spurs Thailand to Fast-Track Long-Standing Landbridge Project

author: Jan Bratanic
description: Slovenian Prime Minister Robert Golob said he’s unable to form a new coalition, opening the door for a political comeback by his nationalist rival Janez Jansa.
title: Slovenia in Political Turmoil as Golob Fails to Form Cabinet

author: Alan Crawford
description: The beleaguered chancellor just can’t seem to catch a break.
title: Like the Stranded Whale Captivating Germany, Merz Looks Beached

author: Eltaf Najafizada, Salma El Wardany, Courtney Subramanian
description: Iran held back from saying whether it would take part in further peace talks even after US President Donald Trump said a delegation is on its way to Pakistan, creating uncertainty about whether a breakthrough can be achieved.
title: Iran Hesitant on Talks Even as Trump Says Vance Is on Way

description: Rumen Radev, Bulgaria’s former president who opposes sanctions on Russia and military aid for Ukraine, scored the nation’s most overwhelming election victory this century on Sunday and pledged to turn the page on years of political gridlock and corruption. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports.
title: Bulgaria’s Radev Scores Landslide Election Win

author: Irina Vilcu, Andra Timu
description: Romania was thrown into fresh political turbulence as the largest ruling party withdrew backing for Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, whose fragile coalition government may now be on the verge of falling apart.
title: Romania Faces Fresh Political Crisis With Premier Under Fire
